text:
julia: FYI — onboarding report: two teams hit confusing behavior around Generator.Stream + ctx.WithTimeout. they expect the stream to cancel immediately on timeout but see background handshake retries keep goroutines alive.

andre: can you paste a tiny repro? is it the auth rotate race we saw before or something else?

julia: minimal: start stream with ctx that has a short timeout; background auth refresher rotates token; timeout fires, caller returns, but runtime schedules a retry handshake that blocks on net.Dial and never notices the stream-level timeout.

sam: ugh. users copy-paste the quickstart which uses ctx timeout only. two quick mitigations: (A) expose an explicit Close/Stop on the stream object to force transport teardown, (B) make each handshake derive a per-stream context that the stream cancels on Close/timeout.

karen: ergonomics ask: developers prefer simple range-style APIs. if we introduce an object with Next()/Close() we should provide a lightweight channel shim for a release cycle. also Close() needs to be safe to call concurrently and idempotent.

emily: docs note: update quickstart and sampleapp to always `defer stream.Close()` when using streaming examples. also add a short paragraph about preferring long-lived token providers that rotate on idle, not mid-handshake.

andre: implementation note: make internal handshakes select on both the per-handshake ctx and a close channel (or stream.Cancel()) so blocked net.Dials wake up on Close(). also add test that simulates 401 mid-handshake and a short ctx timeout to catch regressions.

julia: i'll prototype a small StreamReader API: `Next(ctx) (Token, error)`, `Close() error`, `Ctx() context.Context` (read-only, canceled on Close) and a compatibility shim `StreamChan(ctx) <-chan Token`. will include unit tests for goroutine leaks and a stress script in go-sampleapps.

sam: +1. add a metric `active_streams` with model and client labels to help support triage for customer "hang" tickets. internal debug endpoint optional behind env flag.

karen: let's also add a short migration snippet in the generator README showing channel->Next()/Close() conversion and call it out in the release notes.

emily: volunteer to update the sampleapp and quickstart once the PR is up. small UX request: include an example for Resume() pattern showing a WaitGroup and listening on `stream.Ctx()` for background workers to shutdown cleanly.

julia: thanks — I'll open a draft PR with the API shim, tests, sampleapp changes, and docs. tagging @andre for review.

ci-bot: created draft PR julia/stream-reader-ownership (WIP) — build queued

andre: nice, leave a note in the PR linking the reproducer and add the stress runner script under `samples/stream_leak_test`. i'll review tomorrow.
